children: Australia's competition regulator on Wednesday blocked Insurance Australia Group's
planned takeover of RAC Insurance, finding it would likely weaken competition in key insurance markets in Western Australia.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's (ACCC) decision follows a detailed phase two review into the proposed acquisition of the Royal Automobile Club of Western Australia's underwriting business and brand, first floated over a year ago.
The regulator said the acquisition could reduce competition in the supply of motor vehicle insurance and home and contents insurance in Western Australia.
“The acquisition would combine two large insurers, resulting in a substantial increase in IAG’s market share and a significant increase in market concentration,” ACCC Chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb said.

IAG agreed in May last year to acquire RAC Insurance's underwriting business in an A$1.35 billion ($959.85 million) deal expected to add about A$1.5 billion in gross written premium to IAG’s portfolio.
The ACCC added it found insufficient evidence that the deal would motivate IAG to restrict competitors' access to repair services.
It also concluded there was insufficient evidence to suggest the deal would substantially lessen competition in the smash repair services market in parts of Western Australia.

IAG acknowledged the ACCC's decision in a separate announcement and said it would seek public-benefits authorisation, allowing the deal's customer, community and economic benefits to be weighed alongside competition concerns.

"RAC will remain local, and we'll invest in enhancements to benefit the member experience, and continue to deliver high-quality, competitive insurance products and services," IAG CEO Nick Hawkins said.
RAC Insurance did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
IAG shares fell 2.2% in early trade, their lowest since September 10.
